transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I just keep getting stuck on my appearance. Specifically, it's this sagging, uneven look around my jaw and on one side of my face. I really started focusing on it after seeing myself in a bunch of recent family photos, and now I just can't seem to let it go. 

My wife tells me she barely notices anything at all, and my clients at work don't seem to see it either, but... it's just really bothering me.
How much time would you say you spend thinking about this facial appearance issue on a typical day?

I'm not really sure exactly how much time, to be honest. I haven't really timed it or kept track of it like that. 

It's just... it pops into my head throughout the day. Like when I'm getting ready in the morning, or if I happen to catch my reflection in a window at the office. I wouldn't say it takes up my entire day, but I really don't know what it all adds up to.

When you do think about your jaw and facial appearance during the day, what do you typically do? For example, do you find yourself checking the mirror, taking photos of your face, or comparing how you look to other people?

Yeah, I do a few of those things. It usually happens right before client meetings. I'll go check the bathroom mirror, or I'll pull out my phone camera and check it a few times. I find myself trying to adjust the lighting, or maybe messing with my collar and trying to angle my face so the sagging isn't as obvious. 

And as for comparing, yeah, I definitely do that too. I'll catch myself looking at the younger advisors in the office, or guys at gallery events we go to, just comparing my face to theirs. It's frustrating because I'll realize I'm doing that instead of actually focusing on the conversation I'm supposed to be having.

When you're adjusting your collar or trying different angles with your face before meetings, how much would you say these efforts help you feel better about how you look — and how often do you find yourself doing these kinds of things throughout the day?

I'm not really sure how much it actually helps, to be honest. I mean, maybe it gives me a little peace of mind right in that moment... just enough to get me through the meeting. But it doesn't really make the feeling go away completely. 

And as for how often I do it... I really couldn't give you a number. It just depends on the day, I guess. If I have a lot of client meetings, I'll end up doing it more, but I haven't ever kept track of an exact number.
